info.name: City Complaint & Service Request Platform - API v1
info.description:
Auto-generated from the Express + Prisma source in `src/app`.

BASE URL: `{{baseUrl}}` (default `http://localhost:5000`)

### How to use
1. Set `baseUrl`.
2. Run **01 Auth / Login (tester citizen)** (or Admin / Technician) — its test script saves `accessToken` + `refreshToken` into collection variables.
3. Every request inherits collection auth (`Bearer {{accessToken}}`). Public requests override it with `noauth`.
4. Run the requests top-to-bottom inside a folder — creation scripts store ids in variables (`departmentId`, `categoryId`, `complaintId`, `paymentId`, `notificationId`, ...).

### Notes / known problems (verified against source)
- `POST /api/v1/complaints/:id/feedback` and `GET /api/v1/complaints/:id/feedback` are BROKEN: `FeedbackRoutes` is mounted with `app.use('/api/v1/complaints/:id/feedback', ...)` and the sub-router does not enable `mergeParams`, so `req.params.id` is `undefined`. Keep the path variable for readability, but expect a 404 / wrong-complaint behaviour until it is fixed.
- `POST /api/v1/payments/webhook/stripe` always fails with 400 — `req.rawBody` is never captured (`express.json()` has no `verify` hook).
- All `/api/v1/admin/*` routes return 404 — `AdminRoutes` is commented out in `src/app.ts` (line 50).
- `POST /api/v1/complaints` as `multipart/form-data` MUST send the body as a single `complaintPayload` JSON string field, otherwise every field arrives as a string and `latitude`/`longitude` (z.number) fail validation.
- The webhook routes are intentionally unauthenticated (they are not behind `auth()`).

request.description: GET / — public liveness endpoint.
Verifies `notFound` middleware returns 404 JSON.

POST /api/v1/auth/register — public.
Validation: name >= 2 chars, valid email, password >= 6 chars (required for CREDENTIAL provider), phone `+?[1-9]\d{1,14}`, citizen.nid 10-20 chars.
Stores a 6-digit OTP in Redis for 10 min (`citizen-registration-otp:<email>`) and emails it. No DB row is created yet.
Response: 201 `Verification OTP Sent`.

POST /api/v1/auth/register-email-verify — public.
Body: `{ email, otp }` (otp = exactly 6 digits, from the email).
Creates the CITIZEN user + Citizen profile, sets httpOnly cookies and returns `accessToken`/`refreshToken`.

POST /api/v1/auth/login — public. Seeded citizen: `citizen@gmail.com` / `citizen@12345`.
Sets `accessToken` + `refreshToken` httpOnly cookies AND returns them in the body.
POST /api/v1/auth/login — seeded admin: `admin@gmail.com` / `admin@12345`. Overwrites `{{accessToken}}` with an ADMIN token.
POST /api/v1/auth/login — seeded technician: `technician@gmail.com` / `technician@12345`.
POST /api/v1/auth/login — seeded super admin: `superadmin@gmail.com` / `Super@admin12345`.

POST /api/v1/auth/google — public. Body: `{ idToken }` (Google OAuth id token, audience must equal `GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID`).
BUG: unlike `/login`, this handler never calls `setAuthCookies`, so the browser gets no cookies — only the JSON body tokens.

GET /api/v1/auth/me — any authenticated role. Returns user + `citizen` relation (password omitted).
BUG: the token also carries `name`/`role`, and `checkAuth` matches the DB row on `{id, email, name, role}` — renaming yourself (`PATCH /api/v1/users/profile-update`) or having your role changed makes every issued token fail with 401 until you log in again.
POST /api/v1/auth/refresh-token — public; reads the `refreshToken` **cookie** (no body, no Authorization header). Rotates both tokens and resets the cookies.

POST /api/v1/auth/forgot-password — public. Body: `{ email }`. 6-digit OTP stored 5 min in Redis and emailed. Rejects BLOCKED/DELETED/unverified/Google-only accounts (account enumeration via distinct errors).
Note: the response message leaks the submitted email back to the client.

POST /api/v1/auth/reset-password — public. Body: `{ email, otp (6 chars), newPassword }`.
`newPassword` must match `^(?=.*[a-z])(?=.*[A-Z])(?=.*\d)(?=.*[@$!%*?&])[A-Za-z\d@$!%*?&]{8,}$`.
Existing access/refresh tokens are NOT revoked after the reset.

POST /api/v1/auth/register-staff — roles ADMIN, SUPER_ADMIN.
Body: name, email, password (strong regex), role (`TECHNICIAN` | `ADMIN`), phone (BD format), departmentId (uuid, optional), specialization, experience.
Creates the Technician profile automatically when role = TECHNICIAN.
BUG: `actorId` is accepted by the service but never used — no audit log is written for staff creation.
POST /api/v1/auth/logout — any authenticated role. Only clears the cookies; the JWTs stay valid until they expire and there is no Redis blocklist, so a stolen token keeps working.

formdata.description: jpeg/png/webp/gif/avif, max 5 MB. Field name must be exactly `profile-image`.

request.description: PATCH /api/v1/users/profile-image-upload — any authenticated role. `multipart/form-data`, single file in field `profile-image`. Uploads to Cloudinary and replaces `imageUrl` / `imagePublicId`, destroying the previous image.

PATCH /api/v1/users/profile-update — any authenticated role. All fields optional; the Citizen profile is upserted.
BUG: changing `name` invalidates the current access token immediately (see `/auth/me`).

PATCH /api/v1/users/change-password — any authenticated role. Requires `oldPassword`, `newPassword`, `confirmPassword` (must match, and must differ from the old one). Minimum 6 characters — note this is WEAKER than the 8-char+complexity rule used by register/reset. Existing tokens are not revoked.
POST /api/v1/departments — ADMIN, SUPER_ADMIN. name 3-100, code 2-20 `[A-Z0-9_-]+` (stored upper-cased), description <= 500.

query.description: only departments that have a managerId

request.description: GET /api/v1/departments — all authenticated roles. Returns `{ data, meta }` with `manager` (password omitted) and `_count { staff, categories, complaints }`.
GET /api/v1/departments/:id — all authenticated roles. Includes non-deleted `categories` and `_count`.
GET /api/v1/departments/:id/technicians — ADMIN, SUPER_ADMIN, TECHNICIAN. Returns technician users with their Technician profile (specialization, rating, availability, hourlyRate...). Sorted by name.
POST /api/v1/departments/:id/manager — ADMIN, SUPER_ADMIN. Body: `{ userId }` (uuid). Candidate must be ADMIN / SUPER_ADMIN / TECHNICIAN. The user is detached from any other department they managed.
PATCH /api/v1/departments/:id — ADMIN, SUPER_ADMIN. Partial update (name / code / description / isActive).

DELETE /api/v1/departments/:id — ADMIN, SUPER_ADMIN. Soft delete (`deletedAt` + `isActive=false`); blocked when categories exist.
BUG: the code explicitly allows re-creating a department whose name/code already exists on a soft-deleted row, but `Department.name`/`code` are `@unique` in Postgres — the insert will still fail with P2002.

POST /api/v1/categories — ADMIN, SUPER_ADMIN. name 3-100 (globally unique), description <= 500, slaHours int 1-720 (default 48), departmentId (uuid, must be a non-deleted department).
`slaHours` drives `Complaint.slaDeadline` and the SLA dashboard counters.

GET /api/v1/categories — all authenticated roles. No pagination. Returns only `isActive: true` + non-deleted categories with their department and complaint counts.
BUG: admins therefore cannot see (or re-activate) an inactive category through this endpoint.
GET /api/v1/categories/:id — all authenticated roles. 404 when missing or soft-deleted.

PATCH /api/v1/categories/:id — ADMIN, SUPER_ADMIN. Partial update of name / description / isActive / slaHours / departmentId. No uniqueness check on `name` here — a duplicate surfaces as Prisma P2002 -> 400.
DELETE /api/v1/categories/:id — ADMIN, SUPER_ADMIN. Soft delete + `isActive=false`. Existing complaints keep the relation. Same `@unique name` re-creation issue as departments.

body.raw:
{
  "title": "Large pothole on main road",

request.description:
POST /api/v1/complaints — CITIZEN, ADMIN, SUPER_ADMIN.
title 5-200, description 10-2000, address 5-500, latitude -90..90, longitude -180..180, priority LOW|MEDIUM|HIGH|URGENT (default MEDIUM), categoryId (uuid, active category whose department is alive).
`departmentId` + `slaDeadline` are derived server-side from the category. Returns the complaint with `sla` computed and pushes a notification + audit log.

formdata.value: {"title":"Street light not working","description":"The street light in front of the school has been off for two weeks.","address":"Mirpur 11, Dhaka","latitude":23.8041,"longitude":90.3797,"priority":"MEDIUM","categoryId":"{{categoryId}}"}
formdata.description: MUST be a single JSON string field. Plain multipart text fields arrive as strings, and `latitude`/`longitude` are validated with `z.number()`, so the normal multipart form always fails validation.
Up to 5 files, 5 MB each; jpeg/png/webp/gif/avif.

request.description:
POST /api/v1/complaints (multipart/form-data) — CITIZEN, ADMIN, SUPER_ADMIN.
The controller reads `req.body.complaintPayload` first and JSON-parses it when it is a string (`complaint.controller.ts:18-33`), which is how numeric fields survive multipart.
GET /api/v1/complaints/my-complaints — CITIZEN only. Same filters as the list endpoint, always scoped to the caller. Supports `search`, `categoryId`, `departmentId`, `sla` too.
GET /api/v1/complaints/my-assigned — TECHNICIAN only. Scoped to `assignedTechnicianId = me`. Always sorted by `createdAt desc` (sortBy/sortOrder are ignored).

query.description: Searches title, description, address and category name (case-insensitive).

request.description:
GET /api/v1/complaints/search — any authenticated role (all complaints).
BUG: the controller does `{ ...query, search: req.query.q }`, so `?search=` is always overwritten by `?q=`; if `q` is missing, `search` becomes `undefined` and the filter is silently dropped.
Declared AFTER `/my-complaints` etc. but BEFORE `/:id`, which is what keeps it from being swallowed by `/:id`.

query.description: SUBMITTED | UNDER_REVIEW | ASSIGNED | IN_PROGRESS | RESOLVED | CLOSED | REJECTED | CANCELLED
ON_TRACK | APPROACHING | BREACHED | COMPLETED_ON_TIME | COMPLETED_LATE | PENDING

request.description:
GET /api/v1/complaints — CITIZEN sees only their own; ADMIN/SUPER_ADMIN see all; TECHNICIAN sees assigned OR **any complaint of any department**.
SECURITY BUG (`complaint.service.ts:184`): the technician scope is `OR: [{ assignedTechnicianId: me }, { departmentId: { not: null } }]` — the second branch matches virtually every complaint, so a technician can read the whole complaint list (including other citizens' addresses/descriptions).
BUG: `sla` is filtered AFTER `skip/take`, so page sizes and `meta.total` become wrong whenever `sla` is used.

GET /api/v1/complaints/:id — any authenticated role. 403 for a citizen who does not own it or a technician who is not assigned. Returns attachments, assignments, updates, payments, feedback, `_count` and the computed `sla` object.
GET /api/v1/complaints/:id/updates — any authenticated role with access. `ComplaintUpdate` rows (status notes + manual notes) newest first, each with its author (password omitted).

PATCH /api/v1/complaints/:id — any authenticated role with access. title / description / address / latitude / longitude / priority.
A CITIZEN may only edit while the complaint is `SUBMITTED` or `UNDER_REVIEW`; admins/technicians have no such restriction.
`categoryId` and `departmentId` cannot be changed after creation.

DELETE /api/v1/complaints/:id — any authenticated role with access. Sets `deletedAt` (soft delete), keeping the row for audit.
A citizen can only delete while the status is SUBMITTED / UNDER_REVIEW / ASSIGNED / IN_PROGRESS and while no PENDING/PAID payment exists.
MISSING GUARD: the route has no role filter, so a TECHNICIAN assigned to the complaint can soft-delete it.

PATCH /api/v1/complaints/:id/status — ADMIN/SUPER_ADMIN or the assigned TECHNICIAN (a citizen gets 403).
Legal transitions — admin: SUBMITTED->UNDER_REVIEW|REJECTED, UNDER_REVIEW->REJECTED, RESOLVED->CLOSED. technician: ASSIGNED->IN_PROGRESS, IN_PROGRESS->RESOLVED.
`note` (optional, <=1000) becomes the timeline message. On RESOLVED the assignment is completed, the technician is freed, `resolvedAt` is set and the citizen is notified — all inside one transaction.

POST /api/v1/complaints/:id/assign — ADMIN, SUPER_ADMIN. Body: `{ technicianId }` (uuid, role TECHNICIAN, not deleted, same department when both are set).
Sets status = ASSIGNED, marks the technician BUSY, rejects any previous PENDING assignment, and notifies both sides.
BUG: the service checks the user exists but not that a Technician row exists, so `tx.technician.update` can fail with P2025 for a technician without a profile.

POST /api/v1/complaints/:id/accept — TECHNICIAN only, and only the technician the complaint is assigned to, while status = ASSIGNED. Flips the assignment to ACCEPTED, sets status = IN_PROGRESS, adds a timeline entry and notifies the citizen.

POST /api/v1/complaints/:id/cancel — any authenticated role with access. Allowed only from SUBMITTED / UNDER_REVIEW / ASSIGNED / IN_PROGRESS. Rejects open assignments, frees the technician and sets status = CANCELLED.
NOTE: unlike `/delete`, cancelling does NOT check for an active PENDING/PAID payment, so a paid complaint can be cancelled without a refund.

POST /api/v1/complaints/:id/notes — any authenticated role with access. `message` 3-2000 chars, optional `status`.
BUG: `status` here only tags the timeline row — it does NOT change `Complaint.status` and is not validated against the transition map, so notes can claim any status.

POST /api/v1/complaints/:id/attachments — any authenticated role with access. `multipart/form-data`, field `images`, up to 5 files / 5 MB. Uploads to Cloudinary and appends `ComplaintAttachment` rows. Returns `{ count, attachments }`.

POST /api/v1/complaints/:id/feedback — CITIZEN (admins also pass `auth`, but the service rejects non-citizens with 403).
Body: `rating` int 1-5, `comment` <=1000. Only allowed when the complaint is RESOLVED or CLOSED and the citizen owns it; one feedback per complaint. Closes the complaint and notifies the citizen + technician.
** BROKEN ** — `FeedbackRoutes` is mounted via `app.use('/api/v1/complaints/:id/feedback', ...)` without `mergeParams`, so `req.params.id` is `undefined` (verified locally with Express 5). Prisma strips `undefined` from the `where` clause, so the endpoint operates on an **arbitrary complaint** instead of the one in the URL. Fix: `Router({ mergeParams: true })` or add `/:id` to the sub-routes.

GET /api/v1/complaints/:id/feedback — any authenticated role with access (owner citizen / assigned technician / admin). Returns the Feedback row with its author (password omitted), or 404 when there is none.
** BROKEN ** — same `req.params.id === undefined` problem as above; it will return another complaint's feedback (or 404).

GET /api/v1/notifications — any authenticated role. Newest first, each with a slim `complaint` object.
BUG: the service computes `unreadCount` but the controller only forwards `data` + `meta`, so `unreadCount` never reaches the client.
PATCH /api/v1/notifications/:id/read — owner only (the lookup filters by `userId`, so another user's id yields 404).

PATCH /api/v1/notifications/read-all — owner only. Returns `{ updatedCount }`.
Declared BEFORE `/:id/read`, which is what prevents `read-all` from being parsed as an id.

GET /api/v1/payments/gateways — **public** (no `auth()` on this route). Returns `[{gateway: bkash|stripe, label, configured}]`.
For bKash this is `false` with the current `.env`: the code reads `BKASH_BASE_URL` but the file defines `BKASH_SENDBOX_URL`.

POST /api/v1/payments/initiate — CITIZEN, ADMIN, SUPER_ADMIN.
Body: `complaintId` (uuid), `amount` (optional; falls back to `Complaint.serviceFee`), `gateway` (bkash|stripe, default bkash), `callbackURL` (bKash), `successURL`/`cancelURL` (Stripe).
The complaint must be SUBMITTED / UNDER_REVIEW / ASSIGNED / IN_PROGRESS and must not already have a PAID payment. Returns `paymentId`, `merchantInvoiceNumber`, `amount`, `currency` plus `bkashURL` or Stripe `checkoutUrl` + `sessionId`.
BUG: for bKash `callbackURL` falls back to `config.bkash_callback_url` = `BKASH_CALLBACK_URL` (`http://localhost:5000/api/v1`), which is NOT an endpoint of this app — the redirect after payment 404s.

POST /api/v1/payments/:id/execute — owner or admin. Calls bKash `/execute`, then maps `transactionStatus` COMPLETED->PAID, CANCELLED|REFUNDED->CANCELLED, anything else->FAILED, writes an audit log and notifies the payer. Rejects Stripe payments (webhook only). Idempotent: an already-PAID payment returns `alreadyProcessed: true`.

GET /api/v1/payments/:id/status — owner or admin. Polls the gateway: bKash `/payment/status`, or Stripe `checkout.sessions/:id?expand[]=payment_intent` (expired->CANCELLED, paid->PAID, otherwise PENDING). This is the documented recovery path for Stripe when the webhook is unavailable.

GET /api/v1/payments/:id — CITIZEN (own only), ADMIN, SUPER_ADMIN. Note that `/my-payments` and `/admin/all` are declared before `/:id`, so they are not swallowed by it.
NOTE: TECHNICIAN is not in this route's role list but IS allowed on `/my-payments`.
GET /api/v1/payments/my-payments — any authenticated role, always scoped to the caller.
GET /api/v1/payments/admin/all — ADMIN, SUPER_ADMIN. Same filters plus `complaintId`, and it includes the payer object.

POST /api/v1/payments/:id/refund — ADMIN, SUPER_ADMIN. Only a PAID payment can be refunded. `reason` 3-300 chars required; `amount` optional.
** BUG ** — `toAmountString(payment.amount, payload.amount)` returns `payment.amount` whenever it is non-null, so the requested partial `amount` is silently ignored and the FULL amount is always refunded (both gateways).
Also: Stripe refunds use the hardcoded reason `requested_by_customer`, and `refundAmount`/`refundedAt` are stored as `String` columns.

POST /api/v1/payments/webhook/bkash — **public** (no auth, no signature check).
Body/query: `paymentID` (or `paymentId`). It looks the payment up by `bkashPaymentId`, re-queries bKash for the authoritative status and applies it.
`POST /api/v1/payments/webhook` is a duplicate alias of the same handler.
SECURITY: because there is no HMAC/signature verification, anyone who learns a `paymentID` can force a status sync.

POST /api/v1/payments/webhook/stripe — **public**, `Stripe-Signature` header required, signature verified with HMAC-SHA256 over `t.rawBody` and replay-protected via a Redis `stripe:event:<id>` key (7 days, DB fallback).
Handled events: `checkout.session.completed`, `checkout.session.async_payment_succeeded`, `checkout.session.expired`, `payment_intent.succeeded`, `payment_intent.payment_failed|canceled`, `charge.refunded`.
** BROKEN ** — the controller needs `req.rawBody`, but `app.ts` registers plain `express.json()` with no `verify` hook, so `rawBody` is always `undefined` and every call fails with 400 "Raw request body is required for Stripe signature verification". Fix: `express.json({ verify: (req, _res, buf) => { (req as any).rawBody = buf; } })`.
Second bug: `payment_intent.succeeded` events can never be matched — the payment only learns its `stripePaymentIntentId` from a `checkout.session.*` event, so the intent event falls through to `metadata.paymentId` (absent on a PaymentIntent) and is reported as `ignored: true`.

GET /api/v1/admin/users — ADMIN, SUPER_ADMIN.
** Returns 404 ** — `app.use('/api/v1/admin', AdminRoutes)` is commented out in `src/app.ts:50`; the import was removed too, so the module is dead code. Uncomment to enable.

PATCH /api/v1/admin/users/:id/status — ADMIN, SUPER_ADMIN. Body: `{ status: ACTIVE|BLOCKED|DELETED }`. You cannot change your own status, and changing a SUPER_ADMIN requires the caller to be a SUPER_ADMIN.
CAVEAT: setting `DELETED` here does NOT set `isDeleted`/`deletedAt`, so the user stays active everywhere else.

PATCH /api/v1/admin/users/:id/role — **SUPER_ADMIN only**. Body: `{ role }`. Auto-creates the Technician / Citizen profile when missing. You cannot change your own role.
CAVEAT: demoting a TECHNICIAN leaves the Technician row in place, and the target's existing tokens stay valid until they expire (the JWT still carries the old role, though `checkAuth` re-reads `role` from the DB, so old tokens stop matching -> forced re-login).
PATCH /api/v1/admin/users/:id/department — ADMIN, SUPER_ADMIN. Body: `{ departmentId }`. Only TECHNICIAN / ADMIN / SUPER_ADMIN targets.

GET /api/v1/admin/dashboard-stats — ADMIN, SUPER_ADMIN. 15 aggregations in parallel: users by role, complaints by status, 5 recent complaints, SLA breached/approaching (<24h), revenue sum of PAID payments, department/category counts, average feedback rating, top 5 categories by complaint count.
NOTE: `sla.approaching` uses `slaDeadline <= now+24h`, so it also re-counts already-breached-but-unresolved complaints.
GET /api/v1/admin/audit-logs — ADMIN, SUPER_ADMIN. Newest first, includes the acting user. `writeAuditLog` swallows all failures, so entries can be silently lost.
